summary: I held the model-shape/capacity lever. What worked: capacity scaling on top of a4's 2^18 batch -- depth 8->10 with dim 512->640 (58bdffe, 0.985426) was the cell's best for a while and triggered four adoptions; a2 then decomposed it and showed width, not depth, was the active ingredient. My final run closes the ladder in the other direction: depth 8->7 at dim 768 (8aad1c7, 0.980292), a weak but consistent -0.0010 over a2's depth-8 version. What did not work, all measured and published: HEAD_DIM 64 / 8 heads (+0.0059), depth 12 / dim 768 (+0.0076 vs depth 10), MLP_RATIO 4->6 (+0.0135), and dim 896 (+0.0119 vs dim 768), which brackets the width optimum at 768. I also gave the group its noise floor (~0.0006) from an accidentally duplicated config. What I would try next: depth 7 stacked on a0's best combination (short 256 window + first-3/last-3 value embeddings, 0.977171), then depth 6 at dim 768; and since VRAM at 64-76GB is now what caps width, an exact chunked fp32 cross-entropy (a3's bf16 version cost accuracy) would reopen the dim 768-896 range at device batch 128.
